title: Java exception handling diagnostic
goal: Assess exception control flow, checked exceptions, overriding rules, resource closing, suppression, and exception causes.

tasks.prompt: Predict return and exception behavior when finally contains return or throws another exception.
Predict propagation when finally completes normally after try throws.
Select catch clauses and determine reachability when Exception precedes RuntimeException.
Classify IOException, RuntimeException, and Error as checked or unchecked, and apply catch-or-declare rules.
Determine whether unchecked exceptions may appear in throws and whether throws Exception can cover IOException.
Apply checked and unchecked throws rules to overridden methods.
Explain primary and suppressed exceptions in try-with-resources.
Determine resource close order and suppression when multiple close methods throw.
Handle a called method that declares IOException by catch or throws.
Explain why a wrapped exception is passed as the cause and distinguish cause from suppressed exceptions.
Solve a new combined case with IOException, wrapping, finally, and getCause.

observations.observed_result: The learner did not know the initial return case, then correctly applied finally return and finally throw behavior after explanation.
The learner expected propagation but placed it before finally output and needed correction of the execution order.
The learner selected RuntimeException for IllegalArgumentException, but expected a broader catch before a narrower catch to compile.
The learner expected IOException without catch or throws to compile and classified Error as checked.
The learner correctly said unchecked exceptions may appear in throws, but did not know that throws Exception covers IOException.
The learner first attributed an invalid wider throws clause to signature mismatch, then solved narrower and unchecked override variants.
The learner first expected a close exception to replace the try exception, then correctly identified the primary and suppressed exceptions.
The learner first expected resource A to close first, then correctly handled reverse close order and multiple suppressed exceptions.
The learner correctly said the caller must catch IOException or declare it with throws.
The learner described the cause as an exception hierarchy, then distinguished the cause chain from additional suppressed exceptions after clarification.
The learner correctly predicted cleanup output, IllegalStateException propagation, and IOException as the cause in a new combined case.

assessments.assessment: The learner solved several new variants, but needed explanations for finally behavior, checked exceptions, override rules, and try-with-resources suppression.
assessments.uncertainty: Independent evidence does not yet include a complete mechanism explanation for try-with-resources suppression and checked exception override rules.

errors.description: The learner placed exception propagation before finally output.
errors.correction: The finally block completes before the pending exception continues to the caller.

errors.description: The learner expected catch Exception followed by catch RuntimeException to compile.
errors.correction: The narrower RuntimeException catch is unreachable after the broader Exception catch.

errors.description: The learner expected IOException without catch or throws to compile.
errors.correction: IOException is checked, so the code must catch it or declare it.

errors.description: The learner classified Error as checked.
errors.correction: Error and its subclasses are unchecked.

errors.description: The learner attributed an invalid wider throws clause to a signature mismatch.
errors.correction: A throws clause is not part of the method signature used for overriding.

errors.description: The learner expected the close exception to replace the try exception in try-with-resources.
errors.correction: The try exception remains primary and the close exception becomes suppressed.

errors.description: The learner expected the first declared resource to close first.
errors.correction: Resources close in reverse declaration order.

sources.title: Java Language Specification, Section 14.20: The try statement

next_step.reason: Use a new independent task to check try-with-resources suppression and checked exception override rules.

approval.basis: The learner wrote "zatwierdzam" after reviewing the Polish summary and proposed state changes.
